record.original_question: Is the maximal solvable Galois extension Qsolv of Q pseudo algebraically closed, meaning that every absolutely irreducible Q-variety has a Qsolv-rational point? Equivalently, does every absolutely irreducible Q-variety admit a solvable rational point?

evidence.quote: Here, a field K is called pseudo algebraically closed (PAC, see [FJ08]) if every absolutely irreducible K-variety has a K-rational point.

Even worse, while Frey proved that Qab is not PAC, [FJ08, Corollary 11.5.7], it is a long-standing open question whether Qsolv is PAC, equivalently, whether every absolutely irreducible Q-variety admits a solvable rational point.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{Q}$ denote the field of rational numbers with a fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$. Let $\mathbb{Q}_{\mathrm{solv}}$ be the maximal solvable Galois extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ inside $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, that is, the compositum of all finite Galois extensions $L/\mathbb{Q}$ inside $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ whose Galois group $\mathrm{Gal}(L/\mathbb{Q})$ is solvable. A field $K$ is called pseudo algebraically closed (PAC) if every nonempty absolutely irreducible variety $V$ defined over $K$ (i.e. a geometrically integral $K$-scheme of finite type) has a $K$-rational point.

Question: Is $\mathbb{Q}_{\mathrm{solv}}$ pseudo algebraically closed? Equivalently, does every absolutely irreducible variety defined over $\mathbb{Q}$ have a point with coordinates in $\mathbb{Q}_{\mathrm{solv}}$ (a "solvable rational point")?
artifact.category_tag: PAC fields and Galois extensions of Q
artifact.status_search_result: This is a well-known long-standing open problem in field arithmetic. While Frey proved that the maximal abelian extension Q^ab of Q is not PAC, the analogous question for the maximal solvable extension Q^solv remains open: it is unknown whether every absolutely irreducible Q-variety has a solvable rational point. No solution appears in the available literature as of the search.

status_evidence.title: Pseudo algebraically closed field - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: A field K for which every non-empty absolutely irreducible variety has a K-rational point is PAC; examples include separably closed fields and K(i) where K is the maximal totally real extension of Q.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference defines PAC fields and discusses examples; no claim that Q^solv is PAC.

status_evidence.title: Pseudo algebraically closed field - Encyclopedia of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: Definition and basic properties of PAC fields, including known examples among Galois extensions of Q.
status_evidence.claim: No record of a resolution of the PAC question for Q^solv.
